questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages object lifetimes and memory? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A billing run is iterating over an account while another thread calls removeSubscription for one of its subscriptions. What is guaranteed?
choices: The run may read freed memory, because erase destroys the subscription immediately
The removal blocks until the run finishes because the registry mutex is held
The run always charges the removed subscription one last time
The run sees either the old or new set of subscriptions consistently, because it works on a copy or under the account mutex, and any subscription it already holds stays alive

questions.prompt: runBilling hits a PaymentError for one account in the middle of the registry. What happens?
choices: The exception propagates and no later account is billed
The account is added to failedAccounts and the loop continues with the next account
The charge is retried immediately with the same idempotency key until it succeeds

questions.prompt: Why does AccountRegistry::close move the shared_ptr out of the map and call cancelAll after releasing the registry mutex?
choices: To avoid holding the registry lock while taking the account lock, which keeps the lock scope small and avoids lock nesting
Because std::unordered_map::erase requires the element to be moved first
Because cancelAll would deadlock if called while the map is locked, even from the same thread
To make sure the Account is destroyed before the function returns
